text: Expedia, a travel company, gets real-time airline data to adjust cost based on timing and competitors.
Blinkit increases the price of service charges during hours when the demand is very high while lowering during early and late hours.
After hurricane Katrina, the departmental stores sold water bottles at $20 instead of the usual $2.
When England stepped out of the European Union, the country’s economy collapsed leading to an increase in market prices of all items.
In a country like the Maldives, the cost of imported essentials such as rice are unusually high because of the local government’s policies.
Uber has introduced surge pricing for occasions such as high demand or unwillingness of drivers to serve at lower rates.
In times of natural disasters such as earthquakes, companies in the Japanese market use stored stock to serve consumers in need ensuring the pricing to remain consistent.
In times of natural disasters such as storms, companies in the American market increase the price of electricity to unreasonable rates to adjust to high demand.
Fruitsellers increase prices of fruits when the economy isn’t doing very well.
